title: Perturbation Theory for Time-dependent Singular Quantum Systems
authors: Kaya Güven Akbaş, Fatih Erman, O. Teoman Turgut
abstract: We develop a perturbative framework for time-dependent point interactions in quantum systems with purely discrete unperturbed spectrum. In two and three dimensions the point interaction is described through the renormalized resolvent obtained from heat-kernel regularization, while in one dimension the diagonal Green function is finite and no renormalization is required. Time dependence is introduced either through the interaction parameter or through the motion of the support point. In both cases we expand the non-autonomous Hamiltonian in the spectral basis of the corresponding static point-interaction problem and derive the first- and second-order pole shifts, projection corrections, and transition amplitudes. The method is illustrated by explicit examples: point interactions with time-dependent coupling, harmonic oscillators perturbed by moving point interactions, and a particle on a sphere with a moving interaction center. We also discuss the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator with a moving delta potential, showing that in the non-renormalized case the present formulation reduces to the standard time-dependent perturbation theory.
summary: This paper constructs a sophisticated perturbative theory to handle quantum systems perturbed by singular point interactions whose parameters evolve in time. By using renormalization group techniques and spectral expansions, the authors derive systematic formulas for energy shifts and transition probabilities. This framework is crucial for accurately modeling dynamic processes involving localized coupling strengths in quantum physics.
main_problem: The paper develops a rigorous perturbative framework for analyzing time-dependent quantum systems involving singular point interactions.
main_result: It successfully derives first- and second-order corrections to energy poles, projection operators, and transition amplitudes when the interaction is time-dependent or moves spatially.
method: The method relies on expanding the non-autonomous Hamiltonian in the spectral basis of the static point-interaction problem, utilizing renormalized Green's functions derived via heat-kernel regularization for dimensions 2D/3D.
model_or_system: The core model involves singular perturbations ($\delta$-interactions) applied to systems with purely discrete spectra, such as particles on compact manifolds or harmonic oscillators. Time dependence is introduced either by varying the coupling strength or by moving the interaction support point.
key_observables: Pole shifts (energy corrections $\Delta_k^{(n)}(t)$), projection corrections, and time-dependent transition amplitudes ($c_m(t)$).
important_parameters: The renormalization scale parameter ($\mu$ or $M$), the displacement magnitude ($\epsilon$), and the frequency/time dependence of the perturbation.
main_assumptions: The unperturbed Hamiltonian must possess a purely discrete spectrum, and the analysis assumes non-degenerate eigenvalues for simplicity in deriving pole structures.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the static renormalization theory using heat kernels. It then extends this to time dependence by treating the varying scale parameter $\mu(t)$ as a perturbation, leading to iterative calculations of energy shifts and transition amplitudes up to second order.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced mathematical tools for handling non-standard Hamiltonians (singular potentials) in time evolution problems, which is highly relevant for modeling interactions in cold atoms or cavity QED where localized coupling strengths change dynamically.
